about: Every change to the game, newest first. Each update adds its notes here (scripts/site.py builds /patch-notes from this file). Game changes only: no ads, analytics, payments or behind-the-scenes work, and nothing that is not live yet.

notes.title: Curls and comebacks
items: Two new routes for receivers: the curl and the comeback.
The end-around flows: the receiver takes the handoff at full speed and bends round the edge.

notes.title: A taller field
items: On a computer, the field runs down to the bottom of the window at every size.

notes.title: Up next
items: After the daily drive, the end card offers one thing to play next: Survivor, or Versus if you have it.

notes.title: Less to read
items: Home, Pro and the start of each drive are down to what you play: the explanations are a tap away.

notes.title: Fourth down means go
items: A quarterback no longer throws the ball away on fourth down or a two-point try: he gives his man a chance.
A pressured throw no longer looks like a sack: the rusher gets there as the ball goes and pulls up.

notes.title: A won game grades as won
items: Way ahead with nothing any call could change, playing it out right now earns the pass, not an F.

notes.title: No spoilers at the snap
items: The camera follows the play as it happens instead of zooming out to where it ends at the snap, so a deep ball's zoom no longer gives the catch away.
A play's line in the play-by-play shows once the play is over, not while it runs.

notes.title: A cleaner screen
items: The field is clear again: play speed, personnel, formation and ratings are under one ⚙ Options button (open it once and it stays open).
The run screen goes straight to the runs. The blocking choices are under ⋯, like the pass options.
The how-to lines show for your first few snaps, then get out of the way.
The down and distance stay on screen while the play runs, on offense and defense.

notes.title: A bigger field on desktop
items: On a computer the field is bigger now, and the new ⤢ button on the field switches between Standard, Large and Extra large. Your pick is kept on that computer.

notes.title: No more floating passes
items: A short pass picked off near the quarterback, or a missed screen, no longer hangs in the air: he holds it a moment longer and it goes at a pass's speed.

notes.title: Kick it when you want in overtime
items: In overtime you can now kick a field goal on any down once you're in decent range, like 1st and goal, instead of waiting for 4th down.
Tied or down by 1 or 2 late with a likely kick, you can now kneel to run the clock down and kick it as time runs out.

notes.title: Fewer catches in a crowd
items: A clean catch no longer happens with three defenders on the receiver: a pass rusher or a man in his zone near the catch now takes his angle a few yards off.

notes.title: Smoother plays on phones
items: Plays should run smoother on phones, iPhones most of all: the field is no longer redrawn on every frame while the camera holds still, and players standing still aren't moved again.

notes.title: Runs in the open
items: A runner or receiver with the ball no longer eases up in the open: he turns upfield right away and is still running when he gets hit.

notes.title: No more runs backward for no reason
items: A run can no longer turn into a runner going backward on purpose (a punter taking a safety to run out the clock): those real plays are left out of what a run can be.

notes.title: A simpler pass screen
items: The pass screen is simpler: your receivers, the quick throws and Snap, with more of the field in view. Protection, play action and rollouts are under More.
When the rush gets there before your quarterback can throw to the man you picked, the play says so, and a throwaway goes out on that man's side.
Sacks and throwaways no longer hit every pass call on the same snap at once: each call has its own luck, at the same real-life rate.

notes.title: A fix
items: An interception no longer hangs in the air waiting for the defender: he takes it where he can get to it.

notes.title: Honest odds, pass protection and one-tap pass plays
items: A receiver's catch % is now how often that pick is caught on the snap: sacks, scrambles and throwaways count, and so does calling the same route again and again.
Rollouts fixed: a rollout to a receiver was mostly ending in a scramble, sack or throwaway. Now it is at most 15%.
Pass protection: Standard, RB in or Max protect. More blockers mean less pressure and fewer sacks, but the men who stay in can't catch a pass.

📋 Plays: nine one-tap pass concepts (Four Verticals, Smash, Flood, Mesh, Slants, Stick, Dagger, Post-Wheel, Sideline), each drawn from your formation with what it beats. The one that fits the situation comes first, and you can still change any route after.
Phones: the pass and run screens fit with no scrolling. Receivers two to a row, the options as small chips, the big buttons kept big.
The tackler is on screen from the moment he goes for the ball carrier.
Defenders no longer run right by the ball carrier without making the tackle.

notes.title: Sacks, penalties, run blocking and motion
items: A pass to a receiver you picked can be sacked, or end in a scramble or throwaway, at the real-life rate.
Penalties: accept or decline them.
Calling the same pass over and over gets worse: the defense sits on it, and the game tells you after the second time.
Run blocking: Zone, Power, Counter, Duo or Trap, each better against a light box, a loaded box or a blitz.
Motion: swipe a receiver, tight end or back sideways. Against man coverage, his defender follows him; against zone, the linebackers and safeties slide.
Empty and two-back formations are real: plays come from real plays run from that set.
The stats page counts Survivor games and Pro drives in the drives played.
Kicks line up as a real kicking unit.
A fumble recovered out of bounds is shown going out of bounds.
Checkerboard end zones.
A quick throw nobody could get to that falls incomplete is shown as a drop.

notes.title: Challenges, fanbases, replays and rules fixes
items: Challenge a friend from the daily's end card; see how rare your calls were against the crowd; pick your team and see how its fans did.
Who you called it like: the real offensive and defensive play-callers your calls matched.
Replays, the 10-second runoff, pre-snap motion, a weekly Survivor board, and Thursday's featured daily.
A shorter end card, with the details behind See the breakdown.
Who plays: pick the quarterback too. Swapping one player for another at his position keeps the same grouping.
Passes look like what happened: a catch in his hands, and each miss as it was charted.
Rules from player reports: offside is not an automatic first down, punts into the end zone, timeouts where they belong.
Punt return touchdowns happen at the real rate.
Every kick can be blocked, at the real-life rate.
False starts are back, at the situation's real rate.
Punts land on whole yard lines.
A personnel grouping draws from enough real plays, so the same few results no longer repeat.
Survivor's best run follows your account to every phone.

notes.title: Build a scenario
items: Pro: build a scenario with any two team-seasons from 2001 to 2026, in any situation.
Pro: title your scenarios and post them to Community scenarios, with plays and wins.
Get out of bounds is set route by route.
This week's featured dailies.
Teams go by their city everywhere.
If something breaks, the game says so with a Reload button.

notes.title: Fair scores, start over and draw any play
items: A fairer daily score: every call graded the same way, and luck counts for nobody.
Start over: restart a drive mid-play.
Draw the play in every mode: runs, RPOs, the quarterback's drop, your defense and kicks.
The Snap button is always in reach at the bottom of the calls.
A Home screen: today's drive, Survivor, Pro and your stats in one place.
Featured days get a title. Daily No. 8: Arizona at Los Angeles, pick your side.
The computer plays smarter: defensive timeouts, untimed downs, a late hurry-up, fourth downs and onside kicks.
Matchups measured on real plays; every Pro try gets fresh dice.
Pro: historic drives use the real drive's lineup and their era's overtime rules; playoff runs end on a loss.
Pro: lost your code? Enter the email you paid with and it is emailed to you.
Faster loading, and play offline after your first visit.
A reload in the middle of a play picks up right away.
Play the whole game from the keyboard, with better contrast.
Every player and the ball stay on the field on a short field.

notes.title: Badges, leaderboards, friend challenges and the broadcast view
items: Badges, and streak freezes that save a missed day.
Daily and weekly leaderboards by name, and practice drives after the daily.
Friend challenges: your share link carries your score.
Share my week: a picture of your last seven dailies.
A first-drive tour, and Add to Home Screen.
The daily's intro shows today's players, the typical score and the one to beat.
Phones: the broadcast view, with the field filling the screen, the scoreboard on top and the calls in a sheet you can drag down.
Draw a receiver's route on the field; it plays as the closest real route at the depth drawn.
Your defense lines up on the field as you pick it.
A simple-defense switch, and quick-call descriptions on screen.
One-tap quick pass and real screens; get out of bounds shown up front late.
A real pocket in pass protection, breakups at the ball, and punt coverage that runs.
Ball speed by the throw: line drives, lofted deep balls and soft tosses.
Ball carriers stay in bounds unless you ask them out. Catch-and-runs follow the route, and runs head for open grass.
A called kick always gets off, and a timeout never ends the half. Their timeouts are shown before your call, and no snap happens at 0:00.
Stands, cheerleaders and a mascot behind each end zone.
One brag number on the card: outcalled X% of today's players.
Faster loading.

notes.title: Pro, accounts and the end card
items: Pro: famous historic drives with A-to-F grades, playoff runs, and the archive of past dailies.
Pro: a just-played drive from the latest real game, marked with a badge.
The Gauntlet: a one-night contest on the historic drives.
Accounts: sign in with Google or an emailed link. Your stats follow you, your username goes on the boards, plus friend leagues and an optional daily email.
The end of the game: why each call was graded as it was, the real coach by name, a picture to share, and a daily reminder.
The score is mostly your calls, partly the result.
Anticipation throws: the ball meets the receiver as he comes out of his break.
Running backs no longer wait to be tackled.
Spots start from the score before the snap.
No defensive call when the other team kneels out the clock.
Saturday's daily: a college classic, with college overtime.

notes.title: Overtime, personnel, coach match and the 28–3 comeback
items: Coach match: your calls compared with 144 head coaches since 1999, each in his own era.
Personnel: pick 11, 12, 21 or 13. Backups come in, players jog on and off, and plays come from real plays with that grouping.
Overtime in the daily drive, the two-minute warning, realistic long kicks, and a clearer clock.
Run it down: burn the clock to 0:03, call timeout, then kick.
Call the play on a two-point try, trick plays included.
Each kick's make chance shown on its button.
Your score is measured against real play-callers of every skill level.
Your stats: how you call it, with a running tally of your calls against real play-callers in the same spots.
Featured days with their story. Sunday: the 28–3 comeback.
Spots from any season since 2012.
Player ratings blend several seasons of play.
A Screen button on the pass screen.
Incompletions show why they failed, with a defender at the ball. Loss call-outs say how big the loss was.
Tackles look real: the right defender makes the tackle at the right spot.
Stay in bounds when leading late.
The 2MD logo at midfield.
On wide screens the calls sit beside the field; compact receivers on phones.
A fumble after crossing the goal line is a touchdown. A field goal is allowed on any down late.

notes.title: One drive a day
items: One drive a day, the same for everyone, and a stats page with everyone's results.
Jersey numbers on the players, and name tags before the snap.
Trick plays revamped.
Simpler screens and a faster first snap.
Share opens your phone's share sheet, and shared links show a preview.
A welcome screen, your streak on the results, and a share that asks back.
Your score is measured against real play-callers who read the defense's look.
Fixes: Survivor no longer freezes at the end of a game; the first half ends after a try at 0:00.

notes.title: Launch: Two-Minute Drill
items: Call the plays in a real pro football late-game drive. Every snap is a real play of your call, from the same kind of situation.
A playbook of runs, passes, RPOs and trick plays, built from 160,000 real snaps.
Every snap animated on the field at real game speeds, with players moving like real players.
The real teams and lineups of that game, with our own player ratings.
Every call graded on win chance, and you against the real coach.
Tempo control: no-huddle, huddle, spike or kneel.
Defense: read their look and make the call when they have the ball. Kickoffs: onside, deep or touchback.
Pick a receiver and change any route by tapping him on the field, with each receiver's odds shown.
A defense that adapts to your tendencies.
The snap goes at once; your call is graded while the play runs.
Survivor: win each random real game to keep going, with its own leaderboard and overtime.
